research_notes: The frozen official occupation extract provides the backbone of the timeline but only year-level boundaries and no working-hours evidence.
The AlphaBeta acquisition date is exact primary-employer evidence; it does not prove that every preceding or succeeding day was substantive full-time work.
Senior, founder and managing-director titles are not treated as proof of full-time hours.
Potential overlap among Oxford study, LSE research and the December 2007 government appointment remains explicit.

Systematic follow-up2026-10-01 added omitted BCG and Oxford work, unspecified early jobs and writing; identified LSE centre/UNDP duty station, university completion year and Coles divisional details. Repaired event source URL. Totals remain null because no substantive full-time personal interval was found.

Corrected unsupported personal day boundaries based solely on27February2020 acquisition. Exact transaction date retained in evidence; personalAlphaBeta/Accenture transition remains year-level. Neither title, company staffing nor early office arrival proves full-time work. Coles divisional roles belong within existing2010–2014 spell; two-year descriptions do not license exact split dates.

Searched institutional scholarship/college records, university publications, employer acquisition release, ABAC historical release, trade reporting, public interview/event biographies and first speech; LinkedIn profile returned999, other sources usable. BCG,Oxford and pre-Oxford jobs need primary appointment documents. Search homonyms include chemistry/laser/meteorology careers and must not be merged.

Further leads: Brasenose2005/2006 college reports identify John Hicks scholarship and doctorate under2005 records, but course transfer/award versus enrolment dates require careful reconciliation. Candidate endorsement appears in reporting by28March2022 whereas existing record says1April; exact formal appointment versus announcement needs resolution. No publication or report date promoted to employment start.

Second follow-up 2 October 2026: added omitted e61 founder/director role, March 2021–24 March 2022, using organisation announcement and financial statements. Exact resignation in accounts takes priority over secondary narrative implying departure at May election. Governance/nonprofit excluded and Accenture overlap preserved.

Contemporaneous e61 announcement confirms candidacy by 30 March 2022; corrected unsupported 1 April inception to March precision without guessing exact endorsement day. RBA conference profile independently corroborates BCG and Accenture. Full-time, payroll, leave and earlier-job boundaries remain unresolved; next leads are actual personal appointment/cessation documents, not corporate milestones.
